title: Foods to Limit or Cook Thoroughly During Pregnancy
excerpt: Food-safety guidance inspired by CDC/NHS/FDA themes: deli meats, unpasteurized dairy, high-mercury fish, and undercooked foods.
content:
## Introduction
When pregnant, it's essential to choose safe and healthy foods to protect the health of both mother and baby. In this article, we will provide information on foods that pregnant women should limit or cook thoroughly to avoid health risks.

## Foods to Limit
According to health organizations such as the CDC, NHS, and FDA, there are certain foods that pregnant women should limit or avoid eating because they may contain harmful substances or bacteria. Here are some examples:

* Deli meats and hot dogs: These foods can contain listeria, a bacteria that can harm the fetus.
* Unpasteurized dairy products: Unpasteurized dairy products can contain bacteria like E. coli and Salmonella, which can harm the health of both mother and baby.
* High-mercury fish: High-mercury fish like shark, swordfish, and king mackerel can contain mercury, a toxic substance that can harm fetal development.
* Undercooked foods: Undercooked foods like sushi, sashimi, and raw eggs can contain bacteria like Salmonella and E. coli, which can harm the health of both mother and baby.

## Foods to Cook Thoroughly
To avoid health risks, pregnant women should cook the following foods thoroughly:

* Meat and poultry: Cook meat and poultry to an internal temperature of at least 165°F (74°C) to avoid bacteria like Salmonella and E. coli.
* Eggs: Cook eggs to an internal temperature of at least 165°F (74°C) to avoid bacteria like Salmonella.
* Seafood: Cook seafood to an internal temperature of at least 145°F (63°C) to avoid bacteria like Vibrio vulnificus.

## Practical Tips
Here are some practical tips for pregnant women to choose safe and healthy foods:

* Read food labels: When buying food, read the labels to know the ingredients and storage instructions.
* Choose fresh foods: Choose fresh foods and avoid processed or preserved foods.
* Cook food thoroughly: Cook food to the recommended internal temperature to avoid bacteria and toxins.
* Consult a healthcare provider: If you have any questions or concerns about food safety, consult a healthcare provider or a registered dietitian.

## When to Seek Help
If you experience any of the following symptoms, seek medical help immediately:

* High fever
* Abdominal pain
* Diarrhea
* Vomiting

Remember, choosing safe and healthy foods is crucial to protecting the health of both mother and baby. If you have any questions or concerns, consult a healthcare provider or a registered dietitian.
